finding: New job, so there is no live range to compare. Built totals (parts + stated hours x $120-$160/hr, the national middle labor rate used for these checks), for ONE replaceable low-beam bulb: economy 2015 Honda Civic (halogen H11) about $56-$108; midsize 2012 Subaru Legacy (halogen H7) about $83-$127; truck 2016 Ford F-150 with halogen headlights about $55-$109; luxury 2011 Acura TL (xenon HID D2S bulb) about $187-$294. A supportable overall range is roughly $55-$295, with ordinary halogen cars at about $55-$130 and HID cars near $190-$295. The difference between classes is almost all in the bulb: a genuine halogen bulb lists at $28-$47, a genuine HID bulb at $214. How solid the labor times are: the low end everywhere is 0.3 hour, which two makers print for exactly this job (Subaru for one low-beam halogen bulb on the 2010-2012 Legacy and Outback; Lexus for one halogen bulb on the CT 200h and HS 250h). Only the midsize figure is for the example vehicle; for the Civic, the F-150 and the Acura it is a comparable vehicle's warranty time, and warranty times are the low end of what shops bill. The high end everywhere is a parts retailer's general 30-minute do-it-yourself figure, not a book time. No stated time was found for an HID bulb, so the luxury labor is the least certain. No stated time was found for a bulb change on a car that needs the front bumper cover or the lamp assembly removed, so those cars are NOT covered by these totals: the only figures seen were a maker's 0.8 hour for replacing both lamp assemblies with the bumper cover off (Hyundai Elantra) and a news report of 'over an hour' for a Saturn Aura. Parts caveat: the low ends are discounted genuine bulbs on pages that state the part is new; ordinary aftermarket halogen bulbs were seen for less ($11.75 for a Sylvania H11, $56.99 for a Philips D2S) on pages that do not state condition, so they are recorded as cross-checks only and a shop using them could come in a little under these totals. Against the benchmarks: our halogen totals sit well below RepairPal ($181-$213) and YourMechanic ($177-$272); RepairPal's parts figure of $120-$123 is far above any halogen bulb price found and its labor of $61-$90 is about what 0.5 hour costs, so those services appear to price a dearer bulb mix and a minimum labor charge. Many shops bill a minimum charge (often half an hour) for any job, which would put a real halogen quote nearer the top of our range than the bottom. This is an estimate, never a quote and never a diagnosis.
extras: A quote often adds: the bulb on the other side (bulbs are commonly replaced in pairs because the second is usually near the end of its life, and HID bulbs change colour with age); a shop minimum labor charge; diagnosis if a new bulb does not fix it (fuse, wiring, connector, or on HID cars the ballast or igniter, which are separate and dearer parts); a melted bulb connector or pigtail; headlight aiming; shop supplies and sales tax. On cars where the bumper cover, wheel-arch liner or the whole lamp must come out to reach the bulb, labor is higher than shown here. Cars with LED headlights usually have no replaceable low-beam bulb at all: the whole lamp assembly is replaced, which is a different job costing hundreds of dollars per side.
